title: Characteristics of rare variants with large endophenotype-derived effect sizes
bodyHtml:
This interactive table includes variant level information shared in Supplementary Data 1 and 2 from the manuscript "Endophenotype Effect Sizes Support Variant Pathogenicity in Monogenic Disease Susceptibility Genes" published in Nature Communications 2022 by Halford, Morrill et al.

Included in this table are large effect size variants reported in ClinVar with uncertain significance (VUS) or conflicting assertions and large effect size variants not reported in ClinVar at time of data download (11/28/2020). "Large effect size" is defined as having an effect size greater than 0.5 standard deviations of the trait distribution in the UK Biobank, the primary cohort. Please see the manuscript for additional details regarding the inclusion criteria and interpretation of these variants.

Click the "View" button in each row to see more information about each variant.
projectSummary: This interactive table of rare variants and their endophenotype-derived effect sizes accompanies a 2022 publication from Halford, Morrill, et al.
dataTableLegendHtml:
Click on a column header to sort the table by that column. Filter the table using one or more of the filters above:

  • enter a full or partial variant ID or rsID and hit Return
  • select a trait, gene, or ClinVar classification
  • enter a full or partial codon or amino acid change (e.g., "c.437A>G (p.Glu146Gly)") and hit return
  • enter a maximum minor allele count and hit Return
  • enter a maximum minor allele frequency from gnomAD and hit Return
